transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-21 | Start: 16:00 PT | Duration: ~62 mins
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Ava Li (Redwood SE), John Patel (Sequoia Head of ML), Priya Rao (Eng Lead), Marco Diaz (Infra), Leah Summers (Product)

Auto-summary (auto): Kickoff for POC prioritization; focus on selecting 3-4 open models to vet; define success metrics and bench plan; confirm infra and security constraints.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick round of intros, and then we'll jump to your goals for the POC. 
[00:18] John (Sequoia): Hey, thanks. I lead ML; main ask is we need a model that handles clinical summarization with low hallucination and supports short notes in en and es, maybe fr later. Latency target is... uh we want sub-500ms token latency for our typical small summaries, 95th pct. Cost target is also important — we can't blow the budget on inference.
[00:42] Priya: For infra, we prefer VPC-deployed, keys in our KMS. We may need an on-prem option eventually but start with a VPC private deployment.
[00:55] Marco: Also we'll need audit logs, SSO with SAML, and SOC2-ish assurances.
[01:05] Carlos (Redwood): Great. To set expectations, we typically propose a 6-week POC: week 1 ingest + baseline, week 2-3 run model shortlist + bench, week 4 integration tests with latency SLOs, week 5 quality fine-tuning or prompt-engineering iterations, week 6 run pilot and handoff. Is that aligned?
[01:30] Leah: Sounds good. Quick question on data residency — some of our data must stay in EU region depending on customer.
[01:38] Ava (Redwood): We can pin region routing and run a private deployment in the EU; or use Dedicated capacity with region isolation. There's a small perf cost for cross-region fallback, but we can avoid that. 
[01:54] John: Ok. On metrics, our product metric is clinical accuracy: we need >= 88% on our labeled extraction tests and hallucination rate < 2% for critical entities. For latency, 95th < 500ms. For throughput, peak concurrency ~120 QPS across service, typical avg 20 QPS. Token sizes are around 400-900 tokens per request.
[02:20] Maya: Great detail, that's super helpful. For the model shortlist, our recommendation is to prioritize 3 families: an LLaMA-family quantized 13B variant for cost-efficiency, a 30-40B model tuned for instruction following (open instruction-tuned), and a distilled larger model with better safety profiles. We'll include a smaller cheap model as a fallback for burst traffic.
[02:45] John: When you say "safety profile" do you mean guardrails or innate model training differences?
[02:52] Carlos: Both. Some models are trained with more RLHF/safety data and thus hallucinate less. Also runtime features like response filtering and retrieval-augmented generation lower hallucination. We'll test both.
[03:10] Priya: Retrieval — we plan to use internal de-identified docs as context; is Redwood able to do prefix caching and retrieval scoring?
[03:18] Ava: Yes, we support KV cache and prefix caching; albeit the transcript shows 'K V cache' often in our notes, sorry the auto-transcript split it. We also have built-in RAG connectors and similarity search hooks.
[03:33] Marco: On dedicated vs hosted: we need isolation, but cost is a factor. How different will latency be?
[03:40] Carlos: Dedicated reduces multi-tenant jitter; you get more predictable p95 latency. Hosted is faster to launch. We'll show comparative bench numbers: cold start, steady-state, and worst-case degradation.
[03:55] John: Benchmarks — what metrics will you run?
[04:00] Maya: We'll run: exact match / F1 for entity extraction, ROUGE/ROUGE-L for summarization, hallucination rate measured via entity hallucination tests, p50/p95 latency, throughput (tokens/s and QPS), memory/ram usage, and token cost per 1k. We'll also do multilingual eval for en/es and a small fr set.
[04:20] Priya: Can you include latency distributions for long context sizes? Some of our notes are 4k tokens.
[04:25] Carlos: Yes we'll run variable context lengths: 512, 2k, 4k. Note that some open models are optimized around 2k and degrade after that; we'll profile kernel selection and batching.
[04:40] John: Any thoughts on quantization? We prefer int8/4-bit where quality doesn't drop.
[04:45] Ava: We'll include quantization profiles. Redwood Optimize recommendations will suggest quantization points per model with expected quality delta. We'll show A/B of full fp16 vs 4-bit.gpt-like quant. Some models are more robust to aggressive quant than others.
[05:05] Leah: Timeline — you said 6 weeks, but do you need any code from us?
[05:10] Carlos: We'll need a small adapter: a canonical prompt harness and a telemetry export (anonymized). We'll provide a sample harness if you want.
[05:18] John: Yes we'll do that. Also external compliance review — do you have SOC2/ISO docs?
[05:24] Maya: We have an enterprise security pack; will send SOC2 summary and the data flow diagram. Also note, for HIPAA-adjacent use-cases we recommend Redwood Private with customer-managed keys.
[05:38] Marco: For network egress, can traffic be kept within our VPC?
[05:42] Ava: With Private deployment, yes. For Dedicated we can do VPC peering and private connectivity. For hosted, we can do private endpoints but some metadata may still route. We'll detail this in the security sheet.
[05:55] John: Ok good. On model selection, can Redwood provide approximate cost per 1M tokens for each candidate?
[06:02] Maya: Yes we'll include cost estimates per model under typical and peak usage. Expect something like: 13B quantized ~ $X per 1M tokens, 30-40B ~ 2-3x that, heavy safety tuned model ~ +10-20% cost for the same throughput depending on kernel efficiency. We'll produce a cost vs quality graph.
[06:25] Priya: For evaluation material, we'll provide 300 labeled items for entity extraction and 150 gold summaries for ROUGE. Is that enough?
[06:33] Carlos: That's perfect. We'll add a small holdout for multilingual.
[06:37] Maya: Ok I'll send the shortlist we discussed. Proposed shortlist (prelim): 1) Q-13B-instr (quantized LLaMA derived) - low cost fallback; 2) Bloomz-30B-instr-like - balanced quality; 3) LMed or clinical-tuned 34B variant - best quality on medical domain; 4) Distilled 7B safety-hardened - cheap burst capacity. We'll include exact model names and links in the sheet.
[07:07] John: LMed — is that open? Licensing-wise is it ok?
[07:12] Maya: We'll verify license and note any export restrictions; anything problematic we'll flag.
[07:16] Marco: Will you run the models in our EU region?
[07:19] Carlos: Yes, we can spin Dedicated or Private in eu-west region; that will be part of the infra sync.
[07:30] Leah: How will we handle rollback if quality regresses during rollout?
[07:34] Ava: Redwood has rollout tooling for canary and automatic fallback to previous model variants. We can set automatic thresholds to fail back.
[07:44] John: One more: annotation feedback loop — can we feed corrections back to the system for prompt-tuning or light fine-tuning during POC?
[07:52] Carlos: We can support light fine-tuning and prompt tuning. For privacy, we'd recommend prompt engineering and retrieval first; if you want to fine-tune, we'll discuss data handling and keys.
[08:06] Maya: OK, wrapping up: next steps recap: Maya to send shortlist + bench plan + security pack; John to send telemetry and prompts; Marco to coordinate infra call with Carlos; Priya to share compliance contact. We'll target infra sync early Nov and bench kickoff first week of Nov.
[08:25] John: Good — thanks everyone.
[08:28] (crosstalk, small laughter)
[08:35] Meeting ends
